title: Capacity Onboarding Checklist for New Model Tenants
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This checklist codifies the operational steps, SLO mappings, error-budget allocation, capacity profiles, verification tasks, and monitoring requirements for provisioning new model tenants on Redwood's Hosted and Dedicated inference surfaces. The goal is repeatable, auditable onboarding that preserves SLOs while minimizing cost and blast radius for runtime capacity changes.

When to use this document:
- A product or partner requests a new tenant for model(s) not previously hosted in production.
- Launch of a tenant that will drive >1% of peak request volume or requires private/dedicated GPUs.
- Any customer onboarding that requires a non-default autoscale or quantization profile.

Scope:
- Applies to: hosted API, dedicated pools, and private deployments under Redwood Private control plane.
- Not in scope: internal experimental clusters, pre-production test-only tenants.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: SRE Capacity Team (oncall alias: #sre-capacity-ops).
- Secondary owner: Model Serving Product (paging: model-serving-oncall).
- Escalation path: owner -> team lead -> eng-sre manager -> CTO on-call.

Prerequisites (before starting provisioning)
1) Business sign-off and billing commitment (if Dedicated).
2) Security review completed for tenant (data residency, IAM) — reference: security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/poc-checklist.
3) Model artifact(s) present in "model-catalog" with a verified compatibility profile: architecture, tokenizer, KV cache size, and quantization flags.
4) Template autoscale policy selected (see table below).
5) A dedicated evaluation prompt set and latency budget established by product.

SLO and Error Budget Mapping
- Default SLOs applied to all model tenants unless overridden by contract. Any deviation must be recorded in related_pages and signed off by SRE.

| SLO metric | Default SLO | Rationale | Alert trigger |
|-------------|------------:|-----------|--------------:|
| Availability (successful responses / total) | 99.95% rolling 30d | Protect production customer SLAs | drop below 99.9% for 60m |
| p95 latency (inference.request_latency_p95) | <= 250ms | Interactive experience target | >350ms for 15m |
| p99 latency (inference.request_latency_p99) | <= 1s | Long tail protection | >1.5s for 10m |
| Error rate (5xx) | <= 0.5% | Model runtime failures | >1% for 10m |
| Median cost-per-token (billing.units) | customer-specific target | Cost guardrail | >+50% baseline for 24h |

Error budget allocation guidance:
- New tenant standard allocation: 100% of a sprint's allowable error budget traced to a tenant if it accounts for >5% of service traffic.
- For enterprise/Dedicated: allocate a discrete error budget bucket per tenant. Track in telemetry: telemetry.error_budget.owners = <tenant-id>.

Capacity Profiles (examples)
- Small (dev/proof-of-concept): 1x T4-equivalent vGPU, 2 concurrent inference workers, baseline qps 5, reserve 50% burst.
- Medium (low-latency multi-tenant): 2x A10G-equivalent vGPUs, 8 concurrent workers, baseline qps 50, reserve 30% burst.
- Large (throughput-critical /rush): 8x H100-equivalent vGPUs, 32 concurrent workers, baseline qps 1000, reserve 20% burst.

Provisioning Checklist (numbered steps)
1. Request intake: confirm tenant_id, model_ids, expected qps distribution, region(s), and compliance flags.
2. Select capacity profile (Small/Medium/Large) and autoscale policy (conservative/aggressive/custom).
3. Create tenant record in the capacity registry (internal API): POST /internal/v1/tenants {tenant_id, profile, owner}.
4. Reserve baseline capacity for 72 hours, tag with experiment:onboarding:<tenant_id>.
5. Update routing policy: add tenant to routing table with weight 0.1 for initial traffic ramp.
6. Configure SLO tracking: create a per-tenant SLO object and enable metrics collection for inference.* metrics.
7. Wire up dashboards: instantiate pre-built dashboard template with tenant_id variable and add to the SRE dashboard set.
8. Create alerts and notification rules (see standard alert list below).
9. Run synthetic smoke tests and perf suite (see Testing section).
10. Run a controlled canary ramp per the Rollout gating steps.

Testing and Verification
- Synthetic smoke tests (must pass before >5% production traffic):
  - 50 warmup requests, verify tokenization correctness, no runtime exceptions.
  - 500 payloads against typical prompt set: verify p95 latency < configured target.
- Load test (run against canary/burst absorber):
  - 10-minute ramp to baseline qps. Observe CPU/GPU utilization, request latency, queue length.
  - 3-minute sustained spike to 2x baseline qps to verify burst absorb behavior.
- KV cache correctness: run 100 stateful prompt sequences verifying continuity of kv-cache lookups and memory usage.

Rollout gating (must meet all to continue):
- Smoke tests: pass.
- Load test: p95 < profile threshold and error rate < 0.2%.
- Observability: dashboards show metrics streaming, tracing enabled for requests with trace_id.
- Cost: estimated per-hour spend within 20% of budget for the profile.

Standard alerts to configure (names, metric, threshold, severity):
1. tenant_high_error_rate — inference.5xx_rate > 1% for 10m — sev: P1 (pager)
2. tenant_latency_p95_degradation — inference.request_latency_p95 > target*1.4 for 15m — sev: P1
3. tenant_availability_drop — availability < 99.9% for 60m — sev: P1
4. tenant_capacity_exhaustion — queue_length > workers * 10 for 5m — sev: P2
5. tenant_cost_spike — billing.units/hour > baseline * 2 for 24h — sev: P2

Alert routing and incident response:
- P1 alerts page #sre-pager rotation and post to Slack channel #tenant-ops-alarms with tenant tag.
- On P1, the oncall engineer follows the "model-serving incident playbook" runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/incident-review/model-serving-regression-incident-review-standards-2026.
- For capacity-related P1s, immediately apply pre-approved throttles: update routing weight to 0.0 for non-critical customers and enable fallback to smaller model variant.

Operational tooling snippets
- Reserve capacity (CLI):
  redwood capacity reserve --tenant $TENANT_ID --profile medium --duration 72h --tag onboarding:$TENANT_ID

- Create SLO (curl):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://internal-api.redwood.svc/v1/slo -d '{"tenant_id":"$TENANT","slo_name":"p95-latency","metric":"inference.request_latency_p95","target":"250ms","window":"30d"}'

- Example autoscale policy (YAML):
  autoscale_policy: |
    name: conservative-onboarding
    min_replicas: 1
    max_replicas: 8
    metric: gpu_utilization
    target_percent: 45
    cooldown_seconds: 300

Incident review triggers specific to onboarding:
- Any P1 that occurs within the first 72 hours after initial traffic ramp must run a focused onboarding postmortem. Include: timeline, resource utilization graphs, request traces for 5 failed requests, and root-cause hypothesis.
- Template required fields for onboarding postmortem: problem-statement, impact, timeline, diagnostics run, remediation, follow-ups with owner and due date.

SRE Runbook links (quick reference)
- model-serving-regression-incident-review-standards-2026 (for regressions).
- slo-rollout-readiness-and-capacity-checklist-2026 (read before step 6).
- cross-region-surge-and-emergency-slo-throttle-playbook-2026 (for multi-region tenants).

Cost governance and tagging
- All capacity reserved for onboarding must be tagged: tags = ["owner:<team>", "onboarding:<tenant_id>", "env:prod"].
- Billing alert hooks: if estimated daily spend > $5k for a tenant, finance-notify triggers and account manager is notified.

Operational run cadence and handoff
1. Day 0-3: SRE Capacity oncall actively monitors dashboards; 1-hour check-ins scheduled with product owner.
2. Day 4-14: Review aggregated telemetry daily; reduce reserved capacity if stable after Day 7.
3. After Day 14: move to steady-state capacity governance and error-budget consumption tracked under standard SRE cadence.

Ownership and sign-off checklist (final)
- [ ] SRE Capacity owner confirms smoke/load tests passed.
- [ ] Product owner confirms functional correctness of model outputs.
- [ ] Security approves tenant (if flagged).
- [ ] Billing and finance sign-off for Dedicated commitments.
- [ ] Oncall declares ready for steady-state and removes onboarding tags.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
Q: If a tenant repeatedly breaches its error budget, what happens?
A: The tenant is placed into restricted routing and capacity reduced until remediation is complete. Repeat offenders may incur rate-limits and review with commercial.

Q: Who can request a custom autoscale policy?
A: Product or engineering owners; custom policies require SRE approval and a signed operational runbook.

Change log
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft published by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-02-03: Added autoscale policy examples and testing thresholds (reviewers: Miguel Ortega, Priya Menon).

Appendix: Template smoke test script (bash)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
TENANT=$1
TOKEN="$2"
for i in {1..50}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d "{\"tenant\":\"$TENANT\",\"prompt\":\"Hello world\"}" > /dev/null
  sleep 0.2
done

Notes: store smoke test logs in /var/log/sre/onboarding/$TENANT for 90 days.
